headline: UPDATE TO Komyshuvakha aid-centre strike (recorded toll 53, Nov 6) -- toll rises to 55 on Nov 7 morning
dek: The death toll from Russia's Nov 2 guided-bomb attack on the aid distribution point/shelter in Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia region) rose to 55 on the morning of Nov 7, after rescuers recovered 9 more bodies/remains from the rubble in the previous 24 hours (State Emergency Service, via…
sources: Ukraine State Emergency Service (toll 55, Nov 7); acting Zaporizhzhia governor Mykhailo Semikin (toll 53, Nov 6); HUR (pilot identifications, via Kyiv Post)
fault_line: Russia says it hit Ukrainian military units -- but the bombs fell on people queuing for food, then on the rescuers. Deliberate strike on civilians, or a military target with civilians beside it?

sections.what_happened: The death toll from Russia's Nov 2 guided-bomb attack on the aid distribution point/shelter in Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia region) rose to 55 on the morning of Nov 7, after rescuers recovered 9 more bodies/remains from the rubble in the previous 24 hours (State Emergency Service, via UNN/Censor.net; AP via France 24 relay). Dozens of people remain missing; recovery operation into its sixth day. The strike hit a former school/gymnasium used as a weekly humanitarian aid distribution point and underground shelter as residents queued for aid on Monday; a second strike hit the shelter/rescuers (double-tap): among the dead are 2 rescue workers and 4 police officers. Nine aerial bombs were dropped, including a 3,000-kg FAB-3000 (1.4t explosives). Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) has identified the Russian colonel who planned the strike and six Su-34 pilots who dropped the bombs (Kyiv Post). Russia's MoD says it targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, claiming up to 25 servicemen killed. The UN human rights mission in Ukraine condemned the attack on Nov 3 as likely violating international law. Toll progression: 26 (Nov 2) -> 31 -> 37 -> 40 (Nov 4-5) -> 42 (Nov 5) -> 53 (Nov 6, Semikin) -> 55 (Nov 7, SES). Wikipedia still shows 53 (stale at check time).
sections.what_verified: AP (T1) via France 24 relay (avenews) and Deccan Herald (earlier 42 figure); State Emergency Service of Ukraine is the primary source for the toll figure; UNN/Censor.net/Kyiv Post carry the SES figure but hold NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Russia's MoD: the attack targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha, claiming up to 25 servicemen killed -- no independent evidence offered; the site was a known weekly civilian aid point (every Monday) and the second strike hit rescuers/shelter. Wikipedia infobox still lists 53 killed at check time (lags the SES update).
sections.why_matters: 55 dead at an aid centre -- Russia dropped a 3-ton bomb on people queuing for food, then bombed the rescuers. Ukraine just named the colonel and the six pilots who did it.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO Komyshuvakha aid-centre strike (recorded toll 53, Nov 6) -- toll rises to 55 on Nov 7 morning: State Emergency Service recovered 9 more bodies in 24h; dozens still missing; HUR names the Russian colonel who planned the strike and six Su-34 pilots incl. a FAB-3000 drop; UN rights mission had already condemned the strike

totw_analysis: Our read: 55 dead at an aid centre -- Russia dropped a 3-ton bomb on people queuing for food, then bombed the rescuers. Ukraine just named the colonel and the six pilots who did it. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Russia says it hit Ukrainian military units -- but the bombs fell on people queuing for food, then on the rescuers. Deliberate strike on civilians, or a military target with civilians beside it?
